name: Robert Bellarmine
bio:
Italian Jesuit, born at Montepulciano in Tuscany, who taught theology at Louvain and at the Roman College, was made a cardinal in 1599 and was for three years Archbishop of Capua.

Best known for his Controversies, a defence of Catholic doctrine against the Reformers, he wrote his Explanation of the Psalms late in life, verse by verse, from the Latin Vulgate. He was canonised in 1930 and named a Doctor of the Church in 1931.
